AI Model Settings block for React & shadcn/ui

Add model connects any OpenAI-compatible server, including local ones. It checks the URL, flags a model you already added and tests the connection before adding, showing how long the server took to answer or the reason it failed. The key field hides the key until you show it. Refresh asks your server for the latest catalog and shows a quiet banner such as "2 new models: Nova 3.5 and Atlas 2 Vision", with Show to filter to them. New models arrive off, so nothing changes in the picker until you choose.
Background jobs that get their own model. Pass [] to hide the group.
Base URL, model ID, display name and API key for an OpenAI-compatible server, with a connection test.
Check a custom server. Resolve if it answers and throw with a message if not. Leave it out to add custom models without a test.

Default model opens a menu of the models that are on, grouped by provider, each with its context, cost and abilities. Under the picker, chips show the chosen model's context window, speed and cost, so the tradeoff is visible before anyone opens a chat. Default effort uses the effort slider from Prompt Input and knows what the default model supports. Drag past what it can do and the slider settles on its highest level, the line under it says why, and screen readers hear it too. Models that don't reason grey the slider out and explain that effort doesn't apply.
Each provider and the Pinned group is a list named by its heading, and every row is named by its model.

Every AI product grows a Models page: which models show up in the picker, which one new chats start with, how hard it thinks, and which small model runs the background jobs. Models is that page as one component, ModelSettings, that drops into any Settings section and saves through the same island as the rest of your settings.
Fetch the latest catalog. Models with ids it hasn't seen get a New badge and a banner. Throw to show the reason with Try again. Leave it out to hide the refresh button.
In search with no matches, opens Add model with the query as the model ID.
In search, clears the query.
ModelSettings
Moves between filters. In the effort slider, changes the level, stopping at what the default model supports.
Must be rendered inside SettingsShell, usually in a SettingsSection, because it saves through the shell's save bar.
On a pinned model's switch or menu, moves it up the picker. Alt+↓ moves it down. Focus stays on the same control.

Put ModelSettings inside a SettingsSection. Pass the catalog and what's saved, save in onSave, and return the latest catalog from onRefresh. Throw from either to show the message, and the draft stays.
Save the draft. Throw to show the message in the save bar and keep the draft.
Saves, like the rest of Settings. Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux.
Search, filters, a refresh banner, a Pinned group and one group per provider, each row with a switch and a menu.
Switches are labelled with the model's name and described by its context, cost and abilities. The default model's switch is disabled and says why.

Task models give the explore subagent, chat titles and summaries their own model, or Auto. Nothing saves until you save: every change raises the Settings save bar, Discard puts everything back, including removed custom models, and the default model can't be turned off by accident.

The Models page of an AI product's settings. A default model with its context, speed and cost at a glance, a default effort that knows what each model…
The Prompt Input effort slider, limited to the levels the default model supports.

The catalog. { id, name, provider, context?, speed?, price?, vision?, efforts?, recommendedEffort?, status?, description? }. speed is "fast" | "balanced" | "thorough", price is 1 to 4, efforts lists the effort values the model supports (leave it out for models that don't reason), and status is "new" | "preview".
The cost scale has a text name, such as Low cost, so the dots are never the only signal.
The effort levels, from fastest to smartest.

The model list searches by name, provider and ability, and filters to Enabled, Reasoning, Fast or Vision. Models are grouped by provider with a count of what's on and one switch to turn a whole provider on or off. Each row shows context, a four-dot cost scale and badges for New and Preview. Pin the models you use most from a row's menu and they move to a Pinned group at the top, in the order the picker shows them. Move them with Move up and Move down, or Alt and the arrow keys, without dragging anything.
The whole Models section: defaults, the model picker list and task models. Place it inside a SettingsSection.
Turns the focused model on or off.

What's saved: { defaultModel, effort, enabled, pinned, tasks, custom }. enabled and pinned are model ids, pinned in picker order. tasks maps a task id to a model id or "auto". custom holds the added servers.
When a pinned model moves or a row changes group, focus follows it to the same control.
With reduced motion, the banner, the row highlight and the slider don't animate.
Your own effort levels and tasks
efforts sets the slider's levels, and each model's efforts lists the ones it supports. tasks sets the background jobs that get their own model.

onTestConnection gets the base URL, model ID and key. Resolve when the server answers, or throw with a message people can act on. Add model runs the same test first, so a broken server never lands in the list.
